messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Lack of dark mode causes eye strain",
 "problem_statement": "Users working late-night shifts experience eye strain due to the platform's bright interface. This lack of a dark mode option reduces comfort and usability during extended evening work sessions.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "we’re running claims reports late into the evening and the bright interface is straining our eyes. Any chance we can get dark mode enabled?",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-29T16:20:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We handle a lot of late-night reserves and payments, so eye comfort matters. Let me know if there’s a timeline or workaround.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-29T16:20:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’ll tweak the monitor settings for now and wait for updates on dark mode.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-29T16:20:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re running claims reports late into the evening and the bright interface is straining our eyes — any chance we can get dark mode enabled?",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-29T16:20:00+00:00"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The title and problem statement describe a product usability gap: no dark mode causes eye strain during late-night use. The support quotes from 2026-10-29 explicitly request dark mode as a feature ('any chance we can get dark mode enabled?') and describe a workaround of tweaking monitor settings, both of which count as signal. Nothing indicates the cause lies outside the product, a help article would resolve it, or the feedback is praise. The third quote's monitor-settings workaround further confirms an in-product limitation a squad could address.", "verdict": "pass"}
